literature_evidence.citation: Lin, Goyal, Girshick, He, and Dollar. Focal Loss for Dense Object Detection. ICCV 2017.
literature_evidence.reported_result: Focal loss prevented easy background examples from overwhelming dense one-stage detection and enabled RetinaNet to match or exceed contemporary two-stage accuracy.
literature_evidence.task_relevance: CGL has the same structural imbalance: a small correct set must be ordered above millions of mostly easy background candidates.

literature_evidence.citation: Chen et al. Towards Accurate One-Stage Object Detection With AP-Loss. CVPR 2019.
literature_evidence.reported_result: Replacing classification with a ranking task and optimizing AP-loss improved multiple one-stage detectors without changing their architectures.
literature_evidence.task_relevance: The frozen representation already has good average separation but fails at the fixed-FP ranking tail, so a ranking objective is better aligned than BCE.

literature_evidence.citation: Qian, Chen, Li, and Jin. DR Loss: Improving Object Detection by Distributional Ranking. CVPR 2020.
literature_evidence.reported_result: Distributional ranking addressed foreground/background and background-hardness imbalance and improved RetinaNet ResNet-101 COCO mAP from 39.1% to 41.7%.
literature_evidence.task_relevance: CGL ranks positives against the hard per-video background distribution near the exact FP budget, rather than optimizing average classification.

hypothesis.observed_failure_mode: On the complete fit-train105 44b6 r10/k8 pool, frozen APNCC plus geometry retained only 14/766 known-correct edges (1.83%) at 728/742 FP despite 281/766 correct edges having finite support.
hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: Freeze the released TemporalUNet3D core and train a 135-to-32-to-1 compact edge head with a per-video budget-tail pairwise softplus ranking loss, refreshed against learned hard negatives near each video's deployment FP boundary.
hypothesis.falsification_test: Five deterministic held-video fit-only folds; select the exact per-video top-k under CG0's FP allocation and measure known-correct retention on every full r10/k8 background pool, with 44b6 first.

early_stop_conditions: Reject any input path containing holdout or CV57 before read.
Stop if process-tree memory exceeds 12 GiB, free memory falls below 25%, swap growth exceeds 1.5 GiB, or wall time reaches 360 minutes.
DEAD if held-fit 44b6 retention is below 5% at the exact per-video FP budgets.
PARK if held-fit 44b6 retention is at least 5% but below 15%, or if 6bba retention is below 10%.
success_criteria: Held-fit 44b6 known-correct retention is at least 15% at the exact per-video FP budgets.
Held-fit 6bba known-correct retention is at least 10% and every video respects its exact FP budget.
No validation12, holdout, audit, test, CV57, GPU, Kaggle, RunPod, or graph replay is used.

unchanged_constraints: no GPU, Kaggle, RunPod, submission, graph replay, or full T-03 training

implementation_contract.core: hash-pinned released TemporalUNet3D embeddings already present in the exact V45 r10/k8 sparse caches
implementation_contract.head: Linear(135,32)-GELU-Linear(32,1)
implementation_contract.objective: same-video budget-tail pairwise softplus ranking with deterministic hard-negative refresh
